items.stem: Which member of `IFeed<X>` produces the source snapshot?
items.explanation: A feed implements LoadEntities(), which returns the full snapshot of source POCOs.

misconceptions.b: Create() is a sink member; the feed only reads.

items.stem: In an EF-backed feed, why does `LoadEntities()` end its query with `.ToList()`?

options.text: To materialize the query (run the SQL) while the DbContext is still open and return a concrete snapshot
To delete the source rows after reading
It has no effect and is optional

items.explanation: EF defers execution; .ToList() forces it now, so the SQL runs before the using block disposes the context. (This applies to EF/DbContext sources; an API or file feed already holds concrete data.)

misconceptions.d: Without materializing, enumeration could happen after the context is disposed — a runtime error.

items.stem: Sketch a `CourseFeed` that feeds `Course` from a SQL database queried with EF. Include the [Feed] attribute, the interface, and a LoadEntities() that opens a context, projects rows into Course, and materializes.
rubric: Opens/uses a DbContext and queries it (e.g. .Where/.Select)
Projects rows into new Course { ... } POCOs
Materializes the query with .ToList() (because the source is EF-backed)

items.stem: Your feed returns all 5,000 courses every run. Should you filter it down to 'only the changed ones' yourself?

options.text: Yes — only return rows you know changed
No — return the full snapshot; the engine diffs it against last run and processes only the delta
Yes — otherwise every record is updated every run
No — but you must delete unchanged rows first

items.explanation: Snapshot in, delta out: you emit everything, the engine computes what changed. Unchanged records get NoChangesDetected.

misconceptions.c: Returning everything does NOT mean everything is updated — the engine only acts on real changes.

items.stem: What goes wrong if `LoadEntities()` returns an un-materialized `IQueryable` and the `using` block disposes the DbContext before the caller enumerates it?
rubric: Deferred execution means the SQL runs on enumeration, which now happens after the context is disposed
Result is a runtime error (disposed context); fix is to materialize with .ToList() before returning
items.sampleAnswer: Because LINQ-to-Entities defers execution, the query tries to run when the caller enumerates it — but by then the using block has disposed the context, so it throws. Materializing with .ToList() before returning fixes it.

items.stem: A feed reads its data from the PowerSchool API through an injected provider (not a database). Does its LoadEntities() need the `.ToList()` / open-DbContext handling from the EF example?

options.text: No — that concern is specific to EF/DbContext sources; an API/provider (or file) feed already has concrete data, so you just project and return (e.g. .ToEntityCollection())
Yes — every feed must call .ToList() or it will crash
Yes — feeds only work against SQL databases
No — API feeds can't return a snapshot, so they skip LoadEntities()

items.explanation: The feed contract is the same for any source — return a full materialized snapshot of POCOs — but the EF deferred-execution/.ToList() gotcha only applies when the source is a DbContext. An API/provider feed (like the PowerSchool CalendarCategoryFeed) or a JSON file feed already holds concrete data; it just projects and returns.

misconceptions.b: The .ToList() step is EF-specific, not a universal feed rule.
misconceptions.c: Feeds back onto any source — SQL, an API, or a file — via the same IFeed<X> contract.
misconceptions.d: Every feed implements LoadEntities(); an API feed returns its snapshot from the provider's results.
